detail: 5 graph calls; 1 txns in episode window, 10 memory cases, 1 rare devices

rationale: The disputed $59.67 charge sits comfortably inside this card's own profile: 48/48 prior transactions are online product C, mean $39.80 with a max of $94.70, so the amount is only 0.79 SD above mean (1.5x mean) and well below the card's ceiling. The only structural anomaly is the 'New' device flag on 'Windows | unknown | edge 16.0 | unknown', but the card has already used 13 distinct devices in 180 days, so an unseen browser/device string carries little weight here, and the model itself scored the transaction 0.37. There is no burst (one transaction in the episode window), no card-testing run, no region change, and the rare shared device (Samsung SM-A310F, 6 cards all-time) is not the device used on the flagged transaction and links only to C03938-K1, which carries no confirmed fraud cases. Against that, the customer's dispute and 10 memory cases of confirmed CNP/new-device fraud keep genuine doubt alive, and there is a prior identical $59.67 charge (3368735, 2016-10) suggesting a possibly forgotten subscription-style charge. That mix leaves the case at roughly even before verification, so policy R1 calls for customer validation rather than a block on a single weak signal.
